- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

content.text:
I now have the flagship finding firmly grounded. Component styles live in the 27 `.js` files as shadow-DOM template CSS, and the numbers are stark: **187 hardcoded `px` literals, 0 `clamp()`, 0 container queries, and only 24 `@media` rules across all 27 components** (colour tokenisation, by contrast, is healthy: 656 `var()` refs, only 2 stray hex). The token file itself is entirely fixed-pixel.

Four parallel deep-dives (CSS/tokens, component JS/contract, specs+handover coverage, workflow/structure/conventions) are still running. Here's what I've **personally verified** so far while they finish:

## Confirmed findings (grounded)

**1. The CSS/token system is fundamentally non-responsive — confirmed, and it's deeper than just component CSS.**
- `common.css` defines *every* dimensional token as a fixed `px`: font sizes (`--zimm-font-size-md: 24px` … `4xs: 10px`), line-heights (`32px`, `24px`…), letter-spacing (`-0.12px`), and the whole spacing scale (`2px`–`160px`). No fluid type, no `clamp()` anywhere in the repo.
- Fixed **`px` line-heights** (not unitless multipliers) and **`px` letter-spacing** actively break text resize/reflow — a WCAG 1.4.4 / 1.4.12 concern given your AA target.
- Responsiveness is done by *swapping classes* (`.zimm-text-mobile-body1` vs `.zimm-text-body1`) rather than responsive tokens; headings are locked at 24px at every viewport.
- No breakpoint tokens (768/1280 are hardcoded in media queries); no container queries in a component library that will be dropped into varied layouts; no max-width container token (desktop grid margin is `0px`).

**2. Small but real code-quality bugs in `common.css`:** `.zimm-text-serif` is defined **twice** (lines 321-323 and 402-409) with conflicting properties; `--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey: #969696` hardcodes a hex that already exists as `--zimm-color-grey-300`; motion tokens are explicitly flagged **PLACEHOLDER / "do not treat as final"** while the project heads to build; smallest type token is 10px.

**3. Structural gaps vs the documented workflow:** `03-requirements`, `04-feedback`, and `06-tools` (the MarkItDown MCP home referenced throughout `CLAUDE.md`) **do not exist**. The requirements track has never run.

**4. Writing-convention violations** (repo forbids em/en dashes): real violations in generated content — `specs/components/disclaimer.md` (3), `specs/components/card-editorial.md` (3), `text-input.js`, `viewer.config.js`, `product-detail/index.html`. (Occurrences in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are the rule text itself — not violations.)

**5. Status mismatch:** `05-handover/index.md` says **"Build Status: Design & Requirements Stage,"** yet a full handover exists and a front-end dev lead (you) is already engaged — the flag likely should be "Ready for Build," which also changes how AI agents treat the repo on session start.

I'll fold the four deep-dives' evidence (component-by-component a11y/keyboard gaps, contract integrity, broken handover links, spec coverage matrix, prototype/viewer registration state) into a single categorized report as soon as they land.

- (c) Incomplete skill tables: AGENTS.md/.antigravity.md list ~13 skills and **omit `map-ia`, `stitch-pages`, and `deploy-catalog`**, all of which exist in `.claude/skills/` and appear in CLAUDE.md's 17-skill table.

# Zimmermann Handover Audit — Findings Report

## Framing (read first)

`05-handover/index.md` line 19 declares **`Build Status: Design & Requirements Stage`** — the repo is **not** marked "Ready for Build". So empty platform layers and some gaps are expected for the stage. That said, the audit shows exactly which gaps must close before this is a clean engineering handover. The single biggest issue is **spec coverage: only 15 of 27 catalogued components have a design spec.** Link integrity of `index.md` itself is otherwise very good (all 60+ component/spec/contract/prototype links resolve; only the requirements folder links break).

Scope covered: `05-handover/index.md`, `05-handover/platform/web/*`, all 16 component specs, 1 template spec, the 27-entry contract, all 3 prototype `intent.md` files, `prototypes/INDEX.md`, and all 28 library element folders.

---

## Ranked findings

### 1. Twelve of 27 components have no spec (HIGH)
The contract (`02-design/library/contract/zimm-contract.js`) and library each define 27 components, but `02-design/specs/components/` holds only 16 `.md` files (one of which, `link.md`, maps to no component). Net: **12 catalogued components ship JS + a contract entry + an index row but zero design spec.**

Missing specs (element folder + contract entry exist, spec absent):
`card-baseline`, `cat-links-aside`, `hero-blocks`, `input-action`, `page-toolbar`, `product-detail`, `product-detail-gallery`, `product-detail-options`, `search`, `search-overlay`, `select`, `toolbar-category`.

Evidence: In `05-handover/index.md` the Spec column is blank for these rows, e.g. line 59 `| \`zimm-select\` | ...select.js | | draft |` and line 75 `| \`zimm-search-overlay\` | ...search-overlay.js | | placeholder |`.

Why it matters: several are highly interactive — `zimm-product-detail-options` (size select, add-to-bag, wishlist, accordions), `zimm-search-overlay` (open/close/escape/animation, and flagged `status: placeholder`, "visual design pending"), `zimm-select`, `zimm-search`. A developer has the web-component source and the API contract but no design intent, token rationale, states, responsive behaviour, or a11y notes to build against.
Suggested fix: run `/extract` to generate specs for the 12, prioritising the interactive molecules/organism (`product-detail`, `product-detail-options`, `product-detail-gallery`, `search-overlay`, `toolbar-category`, `search`, `select`).

### 2. PLP and PDP template prototypes have broken `spec:` frontmatter and no spec (HIGH)
The two commerce page templates point at spec files that do not exist:
- `02-design/prototypes/templates/product-listing/intent.md` line 2: `spec: templates/template-product-listing.md` → `02-design/specs/templates/template-product-listing.md` **missing**.
- `02-design/prototypes/templates/product-detail/intent.md` line 2: `spec: screens/product-detail.md` → `02-design/specs/screens/product-detail.md` **missing** (also points into `screens/` while `stage: template`).

Only `templates/main/intent.md` resolves (`template-main-large-screen.md` exists). The `screens/` and `flows/` spec folders contain only `.gitkeep`.

Why it matters: the Product Listing and Product Detail pages are the core of the site. Their prototypes render, but the prototype→spec link dangles and there is no spec layer at all — so measurements are explicitly "not confirmed from Figma" (stated in both intent files) with nothing downstream to confirm them into. This also violates the repo's Missing Path Protocol (dangling `spec:` refs).
Suggested fix: create `template-product-listing.md` and a product-detail template/screen spec (decide `templates/` vs `screens/` and make the frontmatter match), then re-run `/handover` so the Templates table picks them up.

### 3. `index.md` is not a self-sufficient dev entry point — no run/build/setup section (MED-HIGH)
`grep` across `05-handover/` finds no "how to run", local-server, `npx`, prerequisites, or getting-started guidance, and there is no root `package.json`.

Why it matters: the deliverables are ES-module web components, an HTML catalog (`02-design/catalog/index.html`), and HTML prototypes — all of which need a static server to run (ES modules fail on `file://`). `02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` needs Node. A developer opening `index.md` has no instruction on how to serve the catalog/prototypes, what Node version to use, or how to run the validator. `index.md` links source files and the catalog but never says how to view them.
Suggested fix: add a "Getting started / running locally" section to the handover (serve command for catalog + prototypes, Node requirement for `validate.mjs`, where `common.css` must be reachable). Consider a one-line note that specs use a two-layer model and where devs write the platform layer.

### 4. `03-requirements/` folder is entirely absent; three index links are broken (MED)
`05-handover/index.md` lines 135-137 link `../03-requirements/epics/`, `/features/`, `/stories/`. All three 404 — `find 03-requirements` returns nothing; the whole top-level folder is missing. The counts are listed as 0, so content-wise this is empty-by-design, but the links are dead and a CLAUDE.md-mandated top-level folder is gone.
Why it matters: broken links in the canonical entry point erode trust in it; per CLAUDE.md, `03-requirements` is a top-level structural folder.
Suggested fix: recreate `03-requirements/{epics,features,stories}/` (with `.gitkeep`) or have `/handover` render these rows without hyperlinks until the folder exists.

### 5. `link.md` spec is orphaned; `link/` element is a stub (MED)
`02-design/specs/components/link.md` documents the `.zimm-text-link-lg` CSS utility class. It is **not referenced anywhere in `05-handover/index.md`** and appears in no contract entry. Its element folder `02-design/library/elements/link/` contains only `demo.html` — no `zimm-link.js` (confirmed: it is the sole element folder with no JS module).
Why it matters: the spec self-declares `Pattern type: CSS class (not a component)` (line 13), so the missing JS/contract is intentional — but because `index.md` never links `link.md`, a developer using the handover as the single entry point will never discover the sanctioned link styling, and may reinvent it. The stray `link/demo.html` with no module also reads as an abandoned extraction.
Suggested fix: add a "CSS utility patterns" row/section to `index.md` linking `link.md`; either remove the empty `link/` element folder or note it as demo-only.

### 6. All 16 platform layers are empty; template wording has drifted (MED — expected for stage, but a build blocker)
Every spec's Platform layer is a placeholder. Counts: 14 say `[Empty until a developer picks this up.]`, plus one-off variants in `mega-menu.md` (`*To be completed after handover...*`), `product-showcase-blocks.md` (`*Pending handover.*`), and `card-editorial.md` (`_To be completed by the dev team after handover._`).
Why it matters: consistent with `Build Status: Design & Requirements Stage`, so not a defect per se — but since target stacks are web+react and this is heading to build, note that no React/component-mapping or deviation notes exist yet in any spec. The four different placeholder strings indicate `/extract` template drift across dates (a managed-file consistency issue).
Suggested fix: none required until build begins; when standardising, normalise the placeholder string via the `/extract` template.

### 7. `card-editorial.md` embeds a broken screenshot (LOW-MED)
`02-design/specs/components/card-editorial.md` line 107: `![Cards - editorial](assets/2026-07-15-screenshot.png)` resolves to `02-design/specs/components/assets/2026-07-15-screenshot.png`, which does not exist (that folder holds only `2026-07-14-link.png`). The actual image is at `02-design/library/elements/card-editorial/assets/2026-07-15-screenshot.png`.
Why it matters: the only visual reference in the editorial-card spec won't render. Every other spec uses the working `../../library/elements/<name>/assets/...` pattern.
Suggested fix: change the path to `../../library/elements/card-editorial/assets/2026-07-15-screenshot.png`.

### 8. Spec structural inconsistencies — missing sections and boundary markers (LOW)
- **Missing `### Prototype` section** (part of the design layer): `card-editorial.md`, `footer.md`, `link.md`, `product-showcase-blocks.md`, `text-input.md`.
- **Missing closing `<!-- /design-layer -->` marker** (the dev "do not edit above" boundary): `card-editorial.md`, `mega-menu.md`, `product-showcase-blocks.md`.
- **`text-input.md` line 12 declares `Stack: web`** only, while every other spec and the handover declare `web, react`.
- Two visible spec-template generations: older specs use Overview/Tokens/Interactive/States/Variants/Layout/Components/Accessibility/Prototype; newer ones (`text-input`, `card-editorial`, `disclaimer`, `mega-menu`, `product-showcase-blocks`) use Attributes/Typography/Slots/Custom properties/Responsive.
Why it matters: the missing close markers weaken the ownership boundary the two-layer model relies on; the `web`-only stack on `text-input` is likely an oversight.
Suggested fix: re-run `/extract` on the affected specs to restore the standard section set and markers; correct the `text-input` stack.

### 9. Stale reference to removed `zimm-product-card` (LOW)
`index.md` changelog (line 4) records "product-card removed", but `add-to-wishlist.md` line 23 still reads "Used within `<zimm-product-card>` and directly on product pages." No such element/contract entry exists.
Why it matters: points a developer at a component that isn't in the system.
Suggested fix: update the sentence to reference `zimm-card-baseline` / product pages.

### 10. Prototype "template" stage not in declared vocabularies; cosmetic drift (LOW)
`prototypes/INDEX.md` line 7 lists stage values `interaction | flow | tokens | animation` (omits `template`), yet all three registered prototypes use `template` (lines 12-14). `platform/web/annotation-template.md` line 4 omits it too. (CLAUDE.md does permit `template`, so the code is fine; the legends are stale.) Separately, `platform/web/README.md` lines 2/36 reference a skill named `/extract-specs`, but the current skill is `/extract`. Also 4 specs use ASCII `->` vs 12 using unicode `→` in the "Full history" line (both allowed by conventions — purely cosmetic).
Suggested fix: add `template` to the INDEX/annotation legends; rename `/extract-specs` → `/extract` in the web platform README.

# Component JS & Contract Audit — Zimmermann Handover

**Scope:** 27 custom elements in `02-design/library/elements/`, plus `contract/zimm-contract.js`, `validate.mjs`, `README.md`. Read-only. Target: web + react, WCAG AA.

**Validator baseline:** `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` → exit 0, "27 components (14 atoms, 10 molecules, 3 organisms)... Atomic model valid." **It passes, but that green is misleading** — see Finding 4 for what it does not check.

**General pattern (consistency, the good news):** almost every element follows one house style — `constructor` → `attachShadow({mode:'open'})`, `connectedCallback(){ this._render(); }`, `attributeChangedCallback(){ if(old===new) return; this._render(); }`, static `observedAttributes`, one `_render()` that overwrites `shadowRoot.innerHTML`. Shadow DOM is used everywhere. Tokens via CSS custom properties. Deviations are called out below.

---

## Ranked findings (most severe first)

### 1. HIGH — Systemic HTML/attribute injection (XSS) via unescaped `innerHTML` interpolation
Nearly every component interpolates attribute values straight into a template-literal `innerHTML` with no escaping. Two vectors: element injection (text position) and attribute breakout.

Evidence (representative, not exhaustive):
- `banner/zimm-banner.js:82` — `<span class="message">${message}</span>` → `message="<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>"` executes.
- `text-input/zimm-text-input.js:277` — `value="${value}"` (attribute breakout); also `label` at :272, `placeholder` at :278.
- `select/zimm-select.js:32` — `<option value="${o.value}">${o.label}</option>` (options come from a consumer JSON attribute); `product-detail-options/zimm-product-detail-options.js:167` passes `options='${sizeOptions}'` raw.
- `button/zimm-button.js:53-54` — `aria-label="${label}"` and `src="${iconBase}${icon}.svg"` (icon attr breakout).
- `href` sinks with no protocol check (allows `javascript:`): `disclaimer/zimm-disclaimer.js:103`, `card-baseline/zimm-card-baseline.js:155,164`, `page-toolbar/zimm-page-toolbar.js:108`, `product-detail-options/...:176`.

The *only* element that escapes anything is `mega-menu/zimm-mega-menu.js:17` (escapes `<`/`>` on `personal-label` — and even that misses quotes). **Why it matters:** product names, prices, search values, CMS-driven copy, and option lists are exactly the fields that carry untrusted data. **Fix:** central `escapeHtml()` for text positions and quote-escaping for attribute positions, or build DOM via `document.createElement`/`textContent`/`setAttribute` instead of string concatenation. At minimum sanitize all `href` values against an allowlist of protocols.

### 2. HIGH — Shadow-DOM form controls don't participate in forms, and `change` never escapes the shadow root
`zimm-text-input`, `zimm-select`, `zimm-search` render native `<input>`/`<select>` inside their shadow root, expose a `name` attribute, but none are form-associated (`grep formAssociated|attachInternals|ElementInternals` → **NONE**).
- Native form submission does **not** collect shadow-DOM controls, so `name` is non-functional — a `<form>` around `<zimm-select name="size">` submits nothing for it.
- The native `change` event has `composed:false`, so it does **not** cross the shadow boundary. A consumer/React `onChange` on `<zimm-text-input>`/`<zimm-select>` never fires. (`input` is `composed:true` so it does escape — a subtle inconsistency.)
- No component dispatches a `CustomEvent` for value changes (`dispatchEvent` exists only in banner, add-to-wishlist, navigation, search-overlay — none of them the form controls).

This directly contradicts the contract, which states for `zimm-select` (`zimm-contract.js:241`): *"Keyboard navigation, screen reader announcement, and form submission are all native browser behaviour."* Form submission is **not**. **Fix:** make the three controls form-associated (`static formAssociated = true`, `this._internals = this.attachInternals()`, `setFormValue()` on input), and dispatch a documented `zimm-change`/`zimm-input` CustomEvent with `composed:true`, plus a `value` getter/setter (see Finding 5).

### 3. HIGH — Navigation: primary controls are not keyboard-operable (WCAG 2.1.1 / 4.1.2)
`navigation/zimm-navigation.js` handles everything through one delegated `click` listener on the shadow root (`:19`, `_handleClick`). Several controls emit no click from the keyboard:
- **Desktop search trigger** (`:639`): `<div class="search-trigger-field search-trigger" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Open search">`. It is focusable but a `<div>` fires no click on Enter/Space, and there is no `keydown` handler → **not operable by keyboard**.
- **Tablet/mobile utility icons** (`:643-663`): `<zimm-icon type="profile" aria-label="Account">`, `wishlist`, `bag`, and the `search` icon (`:651,660,680`) are bare `<zimm-icon>` (an `<img role=img>`) — **not focusable, not buttons, no tabindex**, yet the search icon triggers `zimm-search-open` on click. Account/Wishlist/Bag are labelled images that look actionable but can't be reached or activated by keyboard or AT.

**Why it matters:** the top-level account/wishlist/bag/search actions are unreachable without a mouse. **Fix:** wrap interactive icons in real `<button>`s (or add `tabindex=0` + `role=button` + `keydown` Enter/Space), and give the search field a `<button>` semantics with key handling.

### 4. HIGH — Contract integrity: `composes` is inaccurate and the validator can't detect it
The validator only (a) checks tiers/composition arithmetic against the `composes` array in the contract and (b) greps `demo.html` for unknown tags. It never parses the element JS, so wrong `composes` data passes silently.
- **`search-overlay` composes are fabricated.** `zimm-contract.js:293` declares `composes: ["zimm-search","zimm-button"]`, but `search-overlay/zimm-search-overlay.js` renders a raw `<input class="search-input">` and `<button class="ok-btn">OK</button>` — it neither renders nor imports `zimm-search`/`zimm-button`. The molecule tier rests on components it doesn't use.
- **Slotted children are listed in `composes`, violating the contract's own Rule B** ("Slotted children are not listed here"). `product-detail` (`:497`), `hero-blocks` (`:430`), `product-showcase-blocks` (`:410`) render *only* `<slot>`s in their templates yet list composed components; `navigation` (`:92`) lists `zimm-mega-menu` (a molecule) which is actually supplied via slots — that slotted molecule is what qualifies it as an "organism". Strictly per Rule B, product-detail composes nothing and navigation composes only atoms.
- **Missing contract entries for real API:** `text-input` renders `<slot name="trailing">` (`zimm-text-input.js:288`, used by `input-action:41`) but the contract lists `slots: []` (`:219`). `mega-menu` observes and styles a `mobile` attribute (`zimm-mega-menu.js:3`, `:122`) not present in its contract attributes (`:166-171`).
- **Validator lower-bound gap:** molecules are allowed to compose nothing. `disclaimer`, `mega-menu`, `toolbar-category`, `product-detail-gallery` are declared molecules with `composes:[]` — under the README's "molecule renders only atoms" definition they're atoms. The `organism` rule enforces "≥1 molecule" but there is no matching "molecule ≥1 atom" check (`validate.mjs:72-82`).

Element-name coverage itself is clean: all 27 contract `element` tags map 1:1 to `customElements.define` calls (verified). **Fix:** correct the four `composes` arrays and the missing slot/attribute entries; extend the validator to (optionally) assert templates against `composes` and to enforce the molecule lower bound.

### 5. MED — No property interface; React-readiness friction
No element defines any `get`/`set` accessor (`grep` → none). Everything is attribute-only.
- Rich data must round-trip through string attributes: `zimm-select options='[{...}]'`, `product-detail-options size-options='[...]'`. React can't pass an array/object prop.
- Boolean attributes are read with `hasAttribute` (e.g. `button disabled`, `inverse`, `full-width`). In React 19 this works, but in React ≤18 `disabled={false}` serializes to `disabled="false"` → `hasAttribute` is true → control wrongly disabled.
- Combined with Finding 2 (no `change`/CustomEvent, no `.value`), wrapping these in React means manual refs + `input`-event listeners. **Fix:** add reflected `value`/`disabled`/etc. property accessors and CustomEvents; consider publishing thin React wrappers.

### 6. MED — Missing ES-module imports for in-template dependencies (inconsistent, fragile)
Components that render other elements in their own template are inconsistent about importing them:
- Self-importing (correct): `input-action` (text-input, button), `product-detail-options` (button, select, add-to-wishlist), `product-detail` (gallery, options).
- **Not importing what they render:** `navigation` renders `<zimm-icon>`/`<zimm-nav-item>` but imports nothing; `banner` renders `<zimm-icon>` (`:84`) with no import; `footer` imports `input-action` but not `zimm-logo`/`zimm-icon` which it also renders (`:278,299-301,323`).

The demos hide this by loading deps as separate `<script type="module">` tags (e.g. `navigation/demo.html` loads `../icon/...` and `../nav-item/...` manually). A dev importing just `zimm-navigation.js` gets un-upgraded icons/nav-items. **Fix:** each element should `import` every tag it renders in-template.

### 7. MED — `search-overlay` modal a11y incomplete
`search-overlay/zimm-search-overlay.js` is a full-screen `position:fixed` overlay (`:57`) but: no `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal="true"`/accessible name on the host; **no focus trap** (Tab leaves the overlay into the page behind it); **no focus restoration** to the trigger on close (`_close` at `:35` just removes the attribute); background is not `inert`/`aria-hidden`. It does get the basics right: Escape closes (`:46`), Enter submits (`:205`), input is focused on open via rAF (`:28,209`), clean `disconnectedCallback` (`:19-22`). **Mitigant:** contract marks it `status: "placeholder"` (`:300`) — but the a11y gaps should be tracked before it ships. **Fix:** dialog role + name, focus trap, return focus, inert background.

### 8. MED — Navigation/mega-menu open with no focus management
When a mega-menu panel or the mobile full-screen menu opens, focus is never moved into the panel, not trapped, and not restored on close. `_updateActiveState` (`navigation.js:268`) only toggles `aria-expanded` and the panel's `aria-hidden`. For the mobile full-screen menu (`:414-423`) this is a WCAG 2.4.3 focus-order problem. **Fix:** move focus to the first panel control on open; trap while open; restore to the trigger on close.

### 9. MED — `zimm-wishlist-change` / `zimm-banner-dismiss` use `composed:false` and get trapped in shadow DOM
`add-to-wishlist/zimm-add-to-wishlist.js:31-34` dispatches `zimm-wishlist-change` with `bubbles:true` but no `composed`. `zimm-add-to-wishlist` is rendered *inside* `product-detail-options`' shadow root (`product-detail-options.js:151`), so the event bubbles within that shadow tree and **stops at the boundary** — a page-level listener never hears wishlist toggles on the PDP. Same pattern in `banner/zimm-banner.js:16`. (Contrast: navigation/search-overlay correctly use `composed:true`.) **Fix:** add `composed:true` to both.

### 10. MED — `nav-item` is a toggle button dressed as a link
`nav-item/zimm-nav-item.js:53` renders `<a href="#" aria-current=...>`. In `navigation`, clicking it toggles a mega-menu panel (it never navigates). So it's a disclosure control marked up as a link with `aria-current` and no `aria-expanded`/`aria-haspopup` — a 4.1.2 role/state mismatch. It also has **no `href` attribute** in its API (observed attrs are only `label`, `active`), so as a standalone atom it can never link anywhere. It also sets `aria-current="false"` explicitly (better omitted) and defines no focus-visible ring (relies on UA default, unlike every other control). **Fix:** for the disclosure use, use `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>`; for a real nav link, add an `href` attribute.

### 11. MED — Full `innerHTML` rebuild on every attribute change
`_render()` replaces `shadowRoot.innerHTML` on each observed-attribute change. Consequences:
- `text-input`: changing `error-text`/`value` while typing destroys the `<input>` and **loses focus and caret** (new node each render, `zimm-text-input.js:47/299`). The typed value is also never reflected to the host.
- Elements that render other custom elements (`product-detail-options`, `input-action`) recreate those children on any parent attribute change — e.g. a `zimm-add-to-wishlist`'s `selected` state or a `zimm-select`'s open state is reset.

**Fix:** build the shadow DOM once; on attribute change, patch only the affected node/attribute rather than re-stamping.

### 12. MED — No `prefers-reduced-motion` handling anywhere
`grep prefers-reduced-motion` → **none**, despite meaningful motion: navigation panel slides + mobile slide keyframes (`navigation.js:399,489-492`), mega-menu enter/close animations (`mega-menu.js:163-189`), text-input floating-label transitions, search-overlay opacity, button/logo-masthead transitions. (WCAG 2.3.3 is AAA, but this is on the brief and is standard.) **Fix:** wrap transitions/animations in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` or neutralize them under `reduce`.

### 13. MED — `card-baseline` with `no-cta` (click enabled) is a mouse-only link

# Component JS & Contract Audit — Zimmermann Handover

**Scope:** 27 custom elements in `02-design/library/elements/`, plus `contract/zimm-contract.js`, `validate.mjs`, `README.md`. Read-only. Target: web + react, WCAG AA.

**Validator baseline:** `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` → exit 0, "27 components (14 atoms, 10 molecules, 3 organisms)... Atomic model valid." **It passes, but that green is misleading** — see Finding 4 for what it does not check.

**General pattern (consistency, the good news):** almost every element follows one house style — `constructor` → `attachShadow({mode:'open'})`, `connectedCallback(){ this._render(); }`, `attributeChangedCallback(){ if(old===new) return; this._render(); }`, static `observedAttributes`, one `_render()` that overwrites `shadowRoot.innerHTML`. Shadow DOM is used everywhere. Tokens via CSS custom properties. Deviations are called out below.

---

## Ranked findings (most severe first)

### 1. HIGH — Systemic HTML/attribute injection (XSS) via unescaped `innerHTML` interpolation
Nearly every component interpolates attribute values straight into a template-literal `innerHTML` with no escaping. Two vectors: element injection (text position) and attribute breakout.

Evidence (representative, not exhaustive):
- `banner/zimm-banner.js:82` — `<span class="message">${message}</span>` → `message="<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>"` executes.
- `text-input/zimm-text-input.js:277` — `value="${value}"` (attribute breakout); also `label` at :272, `placeholder` at :278.
- `select/zimm-select.js:32` — `<option value="${o.value}">${o.label}</option>` (options come from a consumer JSON attribute); `product-detail-options/zimm-product-detail-options.js:167` passes `options='${sizeOptions}'` raw.
- `button/zimm-button.js:53-54` — `aria-label="${label}"` and `src="${iconBase}${icon}.svg"` (icon attr breakout).
- `href` sinks with no protocol check (allows `javascript:`): `disclaimer/zimm-disclaimer.js:103`, `card-baseline/zimm-card-baseline.js:155,164`, `page-toolbar/zimm-page-toolbar.js:108`, `product-detail-options/...:176`.

The *only* element that escapes anything is `mega-menu/zimm-mega-menu.js:17` (escapes `<`/`>` on `personal-label` — and even that misses quotes). **Why it matters:** product names, prices, search values, CMS-driven copy, and option lists are exactly the fields that carry untrusted data. **Fix:** central `escapeHtml()` for text positions and quote-escaping for attribute positions, or build DOM via `document.createElement`/`textContent`/`setAttribute` instead of string concatenation. At minimum sanitize all `href` values against an allowlist of protocols.

### 2. HIGH — Shadow-DOM form controls don't participate in forms, and `change` never escapes the shadow root
`zimm-text-input`, `zimm-select`, `zimm-search` render native `<input>`/`<select>` inside their shadow root, expose a `name` attribute, but none are form-associated (`grep formAssociated|attachInternals|ElementInternals` → **NONE**).
- Native form submission does **not** collect shadow-DOM controls, so `name` is non-functional — a `<form>` around `<zimm-select name="size">` submits nothing for it.
- The native `change` event has `composed:false`, so it does **not** cross the shadow boundary. A consumer/React `onChange` on `<zimm-text-input>`/`<zimm-select>` never fires. (`input` is `composed:true` so it does escape — a subtle inconsistency.)
- No component dispatches a `CustomEvent` for value changes (`dispatchEvent` exists only in banner, add-to-wishlist, navigation, search-overlay — none of them the form controls).

This directly contradicts the contract, which states for `zimm-select` (`zimm-contract.js:241`): *"Keyboard navigation, screen reader announcement, and form submission are all native browser behaviour."* Form submission is **not**. **Fix:** make the three controls form-associated (`static formAssociated = true`, `this._internals = this.attachInternals()`, `setFormValue()` on input), and dispatch a documented `zimm-change`/`zimm-input` CustomEvent with `composed:true`, plus a `value` getter/setter (see Finding 5).

### 3. HIGH — Navigation: primary controls are not keyboard-operable (WCAG 2.1.1 / 4.1.2)
`navigation/zimm-navigation.js` handles everything through one delegated `click` listener on the shadow root (`:19`, `_handleClick`). Several controls emit no click from the keyboard:
- **Desktop search trigger** (`:639`): `<div class="search-trigger-field search-trigger" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Open search">`. It is focusable but a `<div>` fires no click on Enter/Space, and there is no `keydown` handler → **not operable by keyboard**.
- **Tablet/mobile utility icons** (`:643-663`): `<zimm-icon type="profile" aria-label="Account">`, `wishlist`, `bag`, and the `search` icon (`:651,660,680`) are bare `<zimm-icon>` (an `<img role=img>`) — **not focusable, not buttons, no tabindex**, yet the search icon triggers `zimm-search-open` on click. Account/Wishlist/Bag are labelled images that look actionable but can't be reached or activated by keyboard or AT.

**Why it matters:** the top-level account/wishlist/bag/search actions are unreachable without a mouse. **Fix:** wrap interactive icons in real `<button>`s (or add `tabindex=0` + `role=button` + `keydown` Enter/Space), and give the search field a `<button>` semantics with key handling.

### 4. HIGH — Contract integrity: `composes` is inaccurate and the validator can't detect it
The validator only (a) checks tiers/composition arithmetic against the `composes` array in the contract and (b) greps `demo.html` for unknown tags. It never parses the element JS, so wrong `composes` data passes silently.
- **`search-overlay` composes are fabricated.** `zimm-contract.js:293` declares `composes: ["zimm-search","zimm-button"]`, but `search-overlay/zimm-search-overlay.js` renders a raw `<input class="search-input">` and `<button class="ok-btn">OK</button>` — it neither renders nor imports `zimm-search`/`zimm-button`. The molecule tier rests on components it doesn't use.
- **Slotted children are listed in `composes`, violating the contract's own Rule B** ("Slotted children are not listed here"). `product-detail` (`:497`), `hero-blocks` (`:430`), `product-showcase-blocks` (`:410`) render *only* `<slot>`s in their templates yet list composed components; `navigation` (`:92`) lists `zimm-mega-menu` (a molecule) which is actually supplied via slots — that slotted molecule is what qualifies it as an "organism". Strictly per Rule B, product-detail composes nothing and navigation composes only atoms.
- **Missing contract entries for real API:** `text-input` renders `<slot name="trailing">` (`zimm-text-input.js:288`, used by `input-action:41`) but the contract lists `slots: []` (`:219`). `mega-menu` observes and styles a `mobile` attribute (`zimm-mega-menu.js:3`, `:122`) not present in its contract attributes (`:166-171`).
- **Validator lower-bound gap:** molecules are allowed to compose nothing. `disclaimer`, `mega-menu`, `toolbar-category`, `product-detail-gallery` are declared molecules with `composes:[]` — under the README's "molecule renders only atoms" definition they're atoms. The `organism` rule enforces "≥1 molecule" but there is no matching "molecule ≥1 atom" check (`validate.mjs:72-82`).

Element-name coverage itself is clean: all 27 contract `element` tags map 1:1 to `customElements.define` calls (verified). **Fix:** correct the four `composes` arrays and the missing slot/attribute entries; extend the validator to (optionally) assert templates against `composes` and to enforce the molecule lower bound.

### 5. MED — No property interface; React-readiness friction
No element defines any `get`/`set` accessor (`grep` → none). Everything is attribute-only.
- Rich data must round-trip through string attributes: `zimm-select options='[{...}]'`, `product-detail-options size-options='[...]'`. React can't pass an array/object prop.
- Boolean attributes are read with `hasAttribute` (e.g. `button disabled`, `inverse`, `full-width`). In React 19 this works, but in React ≤18 `disabled={false}` serializes to `disabled="false"` → `hasAttribute` is true → control wrongly disabled.
- Combined with Finding 2 (no `change`/CustomEvent, no `.value`), wrapping these in React means manual refs + `input`-event listeners. **Fix:** add reflected `value`/`disabled`/etc. property accessors and CustomEvents; consider publishing thin React wrappers.

### 6. MED — Missing ES-module imports for in-template dependencies (inconsistent, fragile)
Components that render other elements in their own template are inconsistent about importing them:
- Self-importing (correct): `input-action` (text-input, button), `product-detail-options` (button, select, add-to-wishlist), `product-detail` (gallery, options).
- **Not importing what they render:** `navigation` renders `<zimm-icon>`/`<zimm-nav-item>` but imports nothing; `banner` renders `<zimm-icon>` (`:84`) with no import; `footer` imports `input-action` but not `zimm-logo`/`zimm-icon` which it also renders (`:278,299-301,323`).

The demos hide this by loading deps as separate `<script type="module">` tags (e.g. `navigation/demo.html` loads `../icon/...` and `../nav-item/...` manually). A dev importing just `zimm-navigation.js` gets un-upgraded icons/nav-items. **Fix:** each element should `import` every tag it renders in-template.

### 7. MED — `search-overlay` modal a11y incomplete
`search-overlay/zimm-search-overlay.js` is a full-screen `position:fixed` overlay (`:57`) but: no `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal="true"`/accessible name on the host; **no focus trap** (Tab leaves the overlay into the page behind it); **no focus restoration** to the trigger on close (`_close` at `:35` just removes the attribute); background is not `inert`/`aria-hidden`. It does get the basics right: Escape closes (`:46`), Enter submits (`:205`), input is focused on open via rAF (`:28,209`), clean `disconnectedCallback` (`:19-22`). **Mitigant:** contract marks it `status: "placeholder"` (`:300`) — but the a11y gaps should be tracked before it ships. **Fix:** dialog role + name, focus trap, return focus, inert background.

### 8. MED — Navigation/mega-menu open with no focus management
When a mega-menu panel or the mobile full-screen menu opens, focus is never moved into the panel, not trapped, and not restored on close. `_updateActiveState` (`navigation.js:268`) only toggles `aria-expanded` and the panel's `aria-hidden`. For the mobile full-screen menu (`:414-423`) this is a WCAG 2.4.3 focus-order problem. **Fix:** move focus to the first panel control on open; trap while open; restore to the trigger on close.

### 9. MED — `zimm-wishlist-change` / `zimm-banner-dismiss` use `composed:false` and get trapped in shadow DOM
`add-to-wishlist/zimm-add-to-wishlist.js:31-34` dispatches `zimm-wishlist-change` with `bubbles:true` but no `composed`. `zimm-add-to-wishlist` is rendered *inside* `product-detail-options`' shadow root (`product-detail-options.js:151`), so the event bubbles within that shadow tree and **stops at the boundary** — a page-level listener never hears wishlist toggles on the PDP. ### 10. MED — `nav-item` is a toggle button dressed as a link

# CSS Quality, Responsiveness & Token Audit — Zimmermann Handover

**Scope audited (read in full):** `02-design/library/common.css` (516 lines), `02-design/library/tokens.md`, 27 web-component `.js` files (shadow-DOM CSS) + 28 `demo.html` inline styles under `02-design/library/elements/`, 3 prototype template `styles.css`, and `02-design/prototypes/_platform/{ios,android}.css`.

**Architecture note:** Elements are Web Components; their real CSS lives in shadow-DOM template literals inside the `.js` files, not in `.css` files. The library is heavily tokenized (783 `var(--…)` references across components/demos). The responsiveness problem is therefore concentrated in **what the tokens themselves resolve to** (fixed px) and in **layout dimensions**, not in components failing to use tokens.

---

## Verdict on the user's claim
**"The CSS still uses static/absolute values instead of responsive values."** — **CONFIRMED**, with nuance.

- **Zero** `clamp()`, `min()`, or `max()` anywhere in the entire codebase (all files, all layers). No fluid type, no fluid spacing.
- **Every** typography and spacing token is a fixed `px` value (54 px literals in `common.css` token definitions alone).
- The only responsive units present (`rem`, `vw`) are almost entirely **demo-harness scaffolding** (`.group`, `.variant-label`, `.dark-swatch` blocks duplicated across `demo.html` files, e.g. `button/demo.html:10-14`), not shipped component CSS.
- Genuine fluidity that *does* exist is limited to layout mechanics: `%` widths (124 uses, mostly `100%`), `100vh` shells, flex/`grid` `fr`, and `aspect-ratio`. So layouts partly reflow, but **type never scales** and **many fixed section/component dimensions never adapt**.

---

## Ranked findings

### 1. No fluid typography — entire type scale is fixed px [HIGH]
`common.css:178-182` defines all five font sizes as static px: `--zimm-font-size-md:24px; --xs:16px; --2xs:14px; --3xs:12px; --4xs:10px;`. Line-heights (`:185-189`) are also fixed px. All 21 named text styles (`tokens.md:199-220`) inherit these. There is **no `clamp()`-based heading anywhere** (0 across all files).
- **Why it matters (web+react, WCAG AA):** Fixed px type with fixed px line-heights weakens WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text) and 1.4.10 (Reflow). A 24px "H1" is small for desktop and won't fluidly adapt across the 360-1440px range the components target.
- **Fix:** Introduce a fluid type scale in `common.css`, e.g. `--zimm-font-size-md: clamp(1.25rem, 1rem + 1vw, 1.75rem);`, and switch fixed line-heights to unitless multipliers.

### 2. Token system has no responsive primitives [HIGH]
`tokens.md` explicitly documents **"Grid / Breakpoints … Not found in the library"** (line ~326) and **"Z-index … Not found"** (line ~316). `common.css` defines no breakpoint custom properties, no fluid-type tokens, and no spacing tokens above the raw px scale (`:201-213`). Grid margins are hardcoded px (`:238-240`: `30px/24px/0px`). Breakpoint values are literals buried in `@media` rules (`common.css:494,501`).
- **Why it matters:** The "absolute values" problem is baked into the token layer itself. Every downstream consumer (including a future React app) inherits fixed px because the source of truth offers nothing else. There is no single place to tune responsive behavior.
- **Fix:** Add `--zimm-bp-*` breakpoint tokens and a fluid type/space scale to `common.css`, then document them in the empty `tokens.md` Grid/Breakpoints table.

### 3. Fixed-pixel layout dimensions that never reflow [HIGH]
Prototype page templates carry hardcoded magic-number dimensions with almost no width breakpoints. In `product-listing/assets/styles.css`: `column-gap:100px` (`:76`), `height:1047px` (`:106`), `height:380px` (`:113`), `height:920px` (`:121`), `height:560px` (`:128`), `width:210px` (`:167`), and `--hero-width: calc(100% - 776px)` (`:99`, with a comment citing fixed 664/676px widths). `product-detail/styles.css` repeats these (`:110,132,138,145,155`) plus `c-swatch{width:48px;height:60px}` (`:97-98`). Critically, **2 of the 3 page templates (`main`, `product-detail`) have zero width/layout `@media` rules** — only `hover`/`prefers-reduced-motion`. Overall 58 hardcoded dimensional px literals (≥2px, excluding breakpoints/hairlines) live in component JS.
- **Why it matters:** A 1047px-tall hero, 100px gaps, and 776px of reserved width won't adapt on tablet/mobile; the page templates delegate all responsiveness to components' internal breakpoints and otherwise stay desktop-fixed.
- **Fix:** Replace fixed heights with `aspect-ratio`/`min()`, gaps with spacing tokens or `clamp()`, and add layout breakpoints to the page templates.

### 4. Inconsistent breakpoints + mixed mobile-first/desktop-first [MED]
Breakpoint values disagree across the codebase: tablet boundary is a consistent `767/768`, but "desktop" is variously **1024** (components: `navigation.js:329,341`, `footer.js:237`, `disclaimer.js:91`), **1280** (`common.css:501` `.zimm-grid` only), and **1440** (via `max-width:1439px` in `hero-blocks.js:61`, `product-showcase-blocks.js:143`). Direction is mixed: `common.css` and several components are mobile-first (`min-width`), while `card-baseline/card-editorial/logo-masthead/hero-blocks` are desktop-first (`max-width`), and `navigation.js` **mixes both** `min-width` and `max-width` (13 `@media` blocks, lines 317-534).
- **Why it matters:** Three different desktop breakpoints mean components change layout at different viewport widths on the same page. No shared tokens to enforce consistency.
- **Fix:** Standardize on one breakpoint set as tokens; pick a single direction (mobile-first recommended).

### 5. Token bypass: hardcoded values where a token already exists [MED]
Despite strong tokenization, components hardcode values that have matching tokens:
- Icon dimensions `width:20px; height:20px` (`button/zimm-button.js:48-49`) — `--zimm-icon-size-lg` is literally `20px` (`common.css:269`). `20px` is the single most-repeated hardcoded dimension (21 occurrences).
- Borders/outlines `1px` (`button/zimm-button.js:42`, many others) — `--zimm-border-width-default:1px` exists (`common.css:266`).
- `border-radius:2px` (`button/zimm-button.js:44`) — no radius token exists at all (`tokens.md` "Border Radius: Not found").
- Hardcoded transition timings not using motion tokens: `0.15s` (`button/zimm-button.js:109`), `400ms` (`logo-masthead.js:23`), `150ms` (`nav-item.js:46`), plus `200ms/300ms` literals that duplicate `--zimm-motion-duration-fast/default` (5 total).
- **Why it matters:** Defeats the point of the token layer; a token change won't propagate, causing drift in a React port.
- **Fix:** Replace literals with the existing tokens; add a radius token.

### 6. Token doc/impl drift between `common.css` and `tokens.md` [MED]
- **Action gap:** `tokens.md:258` documents `--zimm-size-action-gap` = `0px`; `common.css:247` defines it as `16px` (and `button` renders a 16px gap). Direct contradiction.
- **Motion easings:** `common.css:261-263` defines `--zimm-motion-easing-standard`, `-slides`, `-fades`. `tokens.md:167` instead documents `--zimm-motion-easing-out-soft` (`cubic-bezier(0.20,0,0,1)`), which **is not defined in `common.css`** — while `slides`/`fades` (actually used 3 and 5 times in components) are **undocumented**.
- **Duplicated section:** `tokens.md` has two "Motion" sections (lines ~147 and ~294); the first lists values, the second says "Not found in the library."
- **Why it matters:** A dev implementing from `tokens.md` would reference a non-existent easing token and set the wrong action gap.
- **Fix:** Reconcile `tokens.md` to match `common.css`; delete the duplicate Motion section.

### 7. 18 of 27 components have zero media queries [LOW]
Confirmed: `add-to-wishlist, button, cat-links-aside, flag, icon, input-action, logo, mega-menu, nav-item, page-toolbar, product-detail, product-detail-gallery, product-detail-options, search, search-overlay, select, text-input, toolbar-category` have no `@media`. Many are genuinely atomic (icon, flag) so this is acceptable, but layout-bearing ones (`mega-menu`, `product-detail`, `product-detail-options`) relying solely on fixed px is a gap. `common.css` has only 2 media queries (grid utility). Platform files have 0.
- **Fix:** Audit the layout-bearing zero-breakpoint components for mobile behavior.

### 8. `!important` in shadow DOM (7 occurrences) [LOW]
`product-showcase-blocks.js:145,178`, `mega-menu.js:142,153`, `navigation.js:449,527`, `hero-blocks.js:63` — all `display/animation/flex-direction … !important` inside media queries. Shadow DOM has no external cascade to fight, so these override the component's own base rules and signal specificity problems.
- **Fix:** Restructure so the base and breakpoint rules don't collide; remove `!important`.

### 9. z-index magic numbers, no scale [LOW]
Values used: `1` (`card-baseline.js:129`), `100` (`navigation.js:400`, all 3 prototype templates `:32`, `ios.css:131`), `200` (`search-overlay.js:60`). `tokens.md` confirms no z-index token scale exists.
- **Fix:** Add `--zimm-z-*` tokens (base/sticky/overlay/modal).

### 10. Raw colors outside the token layer [LOW]
Genuine un-tokenized colors: `search-overlay.js:169-170` `background:#f5a623; color:#000` (a monospace dev "placeholder-notice" banner — should be removed before handover). `demo.html` files hold 10 raw hex: demo product-swatch colors (`#8B3A2A`, `#D4BBA8` in product-detail demos) and a few `#191919`/`#ffffff` that duplicate `grey-900`/`white` tokens (`logo/demo.html:12-13`, `text-input/demo.html:14-15`). Prototype templates: **0 raw hex** (clean). `ios.css` (23) and `android.css` (30) raw hex are canonical Apple/Material values and acceptable for reference layers. `common.css` (18 hex) is the definition layer — correct. (Note: an earlier naive grep counted 21 hex in demos, but ~11 were `&#8209;` non-breaking-hyphen HTML entities in `icon/demo.html`, not colors.)

### 11. Duplication / drift [LOW]
`common.css:216-229` retains legacy numeric scale aliases (`--zimm-scale-200…1200`) alongside the named scale — two parallel spacing vocabularies (`tokens.md:248` flags the remap of `-1200` from 48px→64px, a silent breaking change for anyone still using it). The mega-menu placeholder block, `.ps`/`.ps-thumb` swatch, sticky-header pattern (`top:68px`, `z-index:100`, `calc(100% - 776px)`) and `column-gap:100px` are copy-pasted verbatim across all 3 prototype `styles.css` — should be shared.

### Platform reference layers (`_platform/ios.css`, `android.css`) — context, low relevance to web build
Both are self-contained guardrail layers with their own namespaces (`--ios-*`, `--md-*`), correctly isolated from `common.css` (they don't redefine `--zimm-*` tokens). However: both freeze their type scales to fixed px (`ios.css:16-26`, `android.css:15-29`) despite iOS "Dynamic Type" being inherently fluid; both have 0 media queries and fixed device frames (`ios.css:107` `width:390px`; `android.css:111` `width:360px`); and neither references `common.css`. For a **web+react** build these are mobile references of low direct relevance, but they reinforce the same fixed-px pattern.

---

## Quantitative summary

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| `clamp()` / `min()` / `max()` fluid functions, all files | **0 / 0 / 0** |
| Font-size tokens defined | 5, **all fixed px** (10-24px), 0 fluid |
| Component `font-size` via `var()` token vs raw px | **54 via token / 1 raw px** (a debug banner) — components tokenize type well; the tokens are the static part |
| px literals in `common.css` token definitions | **54** |
| Hardcoded dimensional px in component JS (≥2px, non-breakpoint) | **58** |
| `@media` breakpoint px declarations in components | 28 |
| Element JS files with **zero** `@media` | **18 of 27** |
| `demo.html` files with zero `@media` | 25 of 28 |
| Page templates with zero width/layout breakpoints | **2 of 3** (`main`, `product-detail`) |
| Distinct "desktop" breakpoints in use | **3** (1024, 1280, 1440) — tablet 767/768 is consistent |
| Layout direction | **Mixed** mobile-first + desktop-first (`navigation.js` uses both) |
| Raw hex vs `var()` — `common.css` (definition layer) | 18 hex / 159 var — correct |
| Raw hex vs `var()` — component JS | **2 hex** (debug banner) / 666 var |
| Raw hex vs `var()` — demo.html | 10 hex / 117 var |
| Raw hex vs `var()` — prototype templates | **0 hex** / 102 var — clean |
| Raw hex vs `var()` — ios.css / android.css | 23 / 30 hex (canonical platform) — acceptable |
| `!important` occurrences | **7** (all shadow DOM) |
| z-index values (no token scale) | 1, 100, 200 |
| Token doc/impl contradictions | **≥3** (action-gap 0px vs 16px; motion easing out-soft documented-not-defined + slides/fades defined-not-documented; duplicated Motion section) |
| Missing token categories (`tokens.md` "Not found") | Breakpoints, Z-index, Border-radius, Shadows |

**Bottom line:** The library is well-architected for *color/spacing/motion tokenization at the component level*, but it is **not responsive by design** — the type and spacing tokens are fixed px, there are zero fluid functions anywhere, breakpoints are inconsistent and untokenized, and page-level layouts rely on fixed-pixel magic numbers. The user's statement is accurate and well-supported by the numbers above.</result>

- **Why it matters:** Three different desktop breakpoints mean components change layout at different viewport widths on the same page. No shared tokens to enforce consistency.
- **Fix:** Standardize on one breakpoint set as tokens; pick a single direction (mobile-first recommended).

### 5. Token bypass: hardcoded values where a token already exists [MED]
Despite strong tokenization, components hardcode values that have matching tokens:
- Icon dimensions `width:20px; height:20px` (`button/zimm-button.js:48-49`) — `--zimm-icon-size-lg` is literally `20px` (`common.css:269`). `20px` is the single most-repeated hardcoded dimension (21 occurrences).
- Borders/outlines `1px` (`button/zimm-button.js:42`, many others) — `--zimm-border-width-default:1px` exists (`common.css:266`).
- `border-radius:2px` (`button/zimm-button.js:44`) — no radius token exists at all (`tokens.md` "Border Radius: Not found").
- Hardcoded transition timings not using motion tokens: `0.15s` (`button/zimm-button.js:109`), `400ms` (`logo-masthead.js:23`), `150ms` (`nav-item.js:46`), plus `200ms/300ms` literals that duplicate `--zimm-motion-duration-fast/default` (5 total).
- **Why it matters:** Defeats the point of the token layer; a token change won't propagate, causing drift in a React port.
- **Fix:** Replace literals with the existing tokens; add a radius token.

### 6. Token doc/impl drift between `common.css` and `tokens.md` [MED]
- **Action gap:** `tokens.md:258` documents `--zimm-size-action-gap` = `0px`; `common.css:247` defines it as `16px` (and `button` renders a 16px gap). Direct contradiction.
- **Motion easings:** `common.css:261-263` defines `--zimm-motion-easing-standard`, `-slides`, `-fades`. `tokens.md:167` instead documents `--zimm-motion-easing-out-soft` (`cubic-bezier(0.20,0,0,1)`), which **is not defined in `common.css`** — while `slides`/`fades` (actually used 3 and 5 times in components) are **undocumented**.
- **Duplicated section:** `tokens.md` has two "Motion" sections (lines ~147 and ~294); the first lists values, the second says "Not found in the library."
- **Why it matters:** A dev implementing from `tokens.md` would reference a non-existent easing token and set the wrong action gap.
- **Fix:** Reconcile `tokens.md` to match `common.css`; delete the duplicate Motion section.

### 7. 18 of 27 components have zero media queries [LOW]
Confirmed: `add-to-wishlist, button, cat-links-aside, flag, icon, input-action, logo, mega-menu, nav-item, page-toolbar, product-detail, product-detail-gallery, product-detail-options, search, search-overlay, select, text-input, toolbar-category` have no `@media`. Many are genuinely atomic (icon, flag) so this is acceptable, but layout-bearing ones (`mega-menu`, `product-detail`, `product-detail-options`) relying solely on fixed px is a gap. `common.css` has only 2 media queries (grid utility). Platform files have 0.
- **Fix:** Audit the layout-bearing zero-breakpoint components for mobile behavior.

### 8. `!important` in shadow DOM (7 occurrences) [LOW]
`product-showcase-blocks.js:145,178`, `mega-menu.js:142,153`, `navigation.js:449,527`, `hero-blocks.js:63` — all `display/animation/flex-direction … !important` inside media queries. Shadow DOM has no external cascade to fight, so these override the component's own base rules and signal specificity problems.
- **Fix:** Restructure so the base and breakpoint rules don't collide; remove `!important`.

### 9. z-index magic numbers, no scale [LOW]
Values used: `1` (`card-baseline.js:129`), `100` (`navigation.js:400`, all 3 prototype templates `:32`, `ios.css:131`), `200` (`search-overlay.js:60`). `tokens.md` confirms no z-index token scale exists.
- **Fix:** Add `--zimm-z-*` tokens (base/sticky/overlay/modal).

### 10. Raw colors outside the token layer [LOW]
Genuine un-tokenized colors: `search-overlay.js:169-170` `background:#f5a623; color:#000` (a monospace dev "placeholder-notice" banner — should be removed before handover). `demo.html` files hold 10 raw hex: demo product-swatch colors (`#8B3A2A`, `#D4BBA8` in product-detail demos) and a few `#191919`/`#ffffff` that duplicate `grey-900`/`white` tokens (`logo/demo.html:12-13`, `text-input/demo.html:14-15`). Prototype templates: **0 raw hex** (clean). `ios.css` (23) and `android.css` (30) raw hex are canonical Apple/Material values and acceptable for reference layers. `common.css` (18 hex) is the definition layer — correct. (Note: an earlier naive grep counted 21 hex in demos, but ~11 were `&#8209;` non-breaking-hyphen HTML entities in `icon/demo.html`, not colors.)

### 11. Duplication / drift [LOW]
`common.css:216-229` retains legacy numeric scale aliases (`--zimm-scale-200…1200`) alongside the named scale — two parallel spacing vocabularies (`tokens.md:248` flags the remap of `-1200` from 48px→64px, a silent breaking change for anyone still using it). The mega-menu placeholder block, `.ps`/`.ps-thumb` swatch, sticky-header pattern (`top:68px`, `z-index:100`, `calc(100% - 776px)`) and `column-gap:100px` are copy-pasted verbatim across all 3 prototype `styles.css` — should be shared.

### Platform reference layers (`_platform/ios.css`, `android.css`) — context, low relevance to web build
Both are self-contained guardrail layers with their own namespaces (`--ios-*`, `--md-*`), correctly isolated from `common.css` (they don't redefine `--zimm-*` tokens). However: both freeze their type scales to fixed px (`ios.css:16-26`, `android.css:15-29`) despite iOS "Dynamic Type" being inherently fluid; both have 0 media queries and fixed device frames (`ios.css:107` `width:390px`; `android.css:111` `width:360px`); and neither references `common.css`. For a **web+react** build these are mobile references of low direct relevance, but they reinforce the same fixed-px pattern.

| Hardcoded dimensional px in component JS (≥2px, non-breakpoint) | **58** |
| `@media` breakpoint px declarations in components | 28 |
